case.case_title: Lerins Peiris v. Neil Rupasinghe, Member of Parliament and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application 126/99 (FR), decided on 19 November 1999

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s right to freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c) was violated when he was prevented from participating in the workshop and assaulted.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that the respondents’ actions interfered with his associational rights, particularly as chairman of an organization involved in the project.
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents denied responsibility for the petitioner’s exclusion and claimed he left voluntarily after persuasion.
key_facts: The petitioner was Chairman of the Muturajawela United Peoples Organization (MUPO).
The petitioner was prevented from participating in a workshop related to the project.
The petitioner was assaulted and forced to leave by respondents acting in official capacity.
The petitioner’s associational rights were linked to his expressive activities.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court emphasized that freedom of association is essential to preserve other individual liberties like free speech and is indispensable for collective advocacy and political diversity.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The respondents’ conduct effectively prevented the petitioner from exercising his freedom of association by excluding him from the workshop and assaulting him, violating Article 14(1)(c).
principles_established: Freedom of association is a matrix for other freedoms including speech.
Collective effort and group association are protected to preserve political and cultural diversity.
Elected representatives must not suppress dissident expression through coercion.
precedents_cited: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People v. Alabama Ex Rel. Patterson
Channa Pieris v. Attorney General and Others
West Virginia State Board of Education v. Barnette

outcome.holding: The court declared that the respondents violated the petitioner’s fundamental right to freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The respondents were ordered to pay compensation and costs as per the judgment.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 14(1)(c) was central because the petitioner’s exclusion and assault interfered with his associational rights as chairman of an organization, which the court found constitutionally protected.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was prevented from participating in the workshop and assaulted, which the court held violated his freedom of association guaranteed by Article 14(1)(c).
